subject: Dedicated GPU SKU: sizing guardrails & canary plan
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: James Hsu <james@aeriumlabs.com>, Sarah Patel <sarah@aeriumlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU SKU: sizing guardrails & canary plan

James / Sarah — thanks for the call today. As promised, I'm putting our recommended approach in a single thread so we can iterate quickly. High-level asks from Aerium: how to size Dedicated for your launch (H100 vs A100 vs L4), memory vs perf tradeoffs, and a safe canary/fallback plan during rollouts.

Quick background (from our notes):
- Expected steady-state QPS: 55 rps median across peak window, 200 rps burst for short windows.
- Model mix: 60% short responses (<128 tokens) on an LLM-optimized retrieval flow, 30% generation tasks (up to 1k tokens), 10% embeddings batch jobs.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 450ms for interactive routes.
- Budget: prefer a cost-efficient baseline with headroom for spikes.

Attachments: [Attachment: aerium_qps_profile.csv (text/csv, 45KB)], [Attachment: proposal_sku_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 120KB)]. The CSV contains the sample QPS by hour you sent; the XLSX includes an initial SKU matrix.

Initial recommendations (summary):
- Baseline: A100 reserved pool sized for the 55 rps median for generation-heavy requests — offers balanced memory/perf for 1k-token runs.
- Burst & cost efficiency: L4 cluster for embeddings and short-context interactive traffic; cheaper per-token and good latency for short sequences.
- High-throughput training/large-batch inference or RL-like workloads: a small H100 reserve for peak batch windows (or can be configured as burstable Dedicated slots) — H100 is the best fit when memory bandwidth and tensor core perf dominate.

Operational guardrails we suggest adding to the Dedicated config:
- Auto-fallback policy: route to L4 for requests below 256 tokens when A100 headroom is low.
- Canary plan: start with 20% traffic on the new Dedicated pool for 48 hours with automatic rollback if p95 > 600ms or error rate increases > 2x baseline.
- KV cache & prefix caching thresholds: pin long-context sessions to A100/H100 to avoid eviction storms; short sessions routed to L4.

Can Ben (solutions) and Dev (infra) add any ops caveats? Marissa — I'll loop you for pricing/term discussion once we agree on the SKU split.

— Irene

Thanks Irene — this is useful. A few clarifications from our side:
- Long-context proportion: the 30% generation includes about half of requests that actually need 800–1k tokens (our summarization flows).
- Embeddings: nightly bulk jobs will spike for 30–60 minutes at 500 rps but are not latency-sensitive.
- Budget: we'd prefer to avoid a large H100 reserved commitment if A100+L4 can be tuned, but we understand the perf benefits.

Question: can you call out an example node mix (counts) for a baseline 55 rps steady-state vs a 200 rps burst window? Also want to understand preference for single-sku vs mixed pools from an ops & SLAs perspective.

— James
James Hsu
Head of ML Platforms, Aerium Labs
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: James Hsu <james@aeriumlabs.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU SKU: sizing guardrails & canary plan

James — good questions. Concrete node-level example below (ballpark; we'll refine with telemetry):

Scenario A — Steady baseline (55 rps median; mixed model lengths):
- 6 x A100 (40GB) nodes reserved: covers generation-heavy p95s with headroom for long-context sessions and KV cache residency.
- 4 x L4 nodes (burst pool / autoscale): handle short-context interactive traffic and embeddings during non-peak windows (also used for cost-savings).
- H100: 0 reserved; 1 x H100 on burst-burst config (preemptible or on-demand burst) for nightly large-batch embedding or RL batch jobs.

Scenario B — Peak/burst tolerant (200 rps short window):
- Keep 6 x A100 reserved + autoscale 3 extra A100 for generation paths (if traffic splits favor long-context generation).
- Autoscale L4 to 12 nodes for the short-path traffic; embeddings batch scheduled to use off-peak slots.
- If embeddings/batch contention is high, spin up 2 x H100 for 2–4 hour window (burst policy).

Tradeoffs:
- A100 (40GB): sweet spot for mixed workloads with long-context. Easier to guarantee KV residency and predictable p95. Cost is mid-range.
- L4: cost-effective for short-context and embeddings; lower memory means it's not ideal for 1k-token runs.
- H100: highest perf for throughput and memory-bound models; best for large-batch or extremely memory-heavy models, but higher $/hour.

Ops preference: a mixed-pool (A100 baseline + L4 for short paths) is the pragmatic starting point. Reserve H100 only if telemetry indicates sustained large-batch windows that justify cost.

Dev note — tagging Dev for infra details: Dev? any constraints on tiling/kv with the proposed split and failover paths?

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated GPU SKU: sizing guardrails & canary plan

Forwarding final ops checklist — incorporated Ben's numbers and added infra caveats. (See below includes quoted thread.)

Key infra caveats / runbook items:
- KV cache affinity: require session pinning for long-context flows to an A100 pool. If sessions get evicted, latency spikes and context truncation will occur. Recommend a TTL-based admit filter (20–30 minutes) for pinned sessions.
- Prefix caching: enable automatic prefix caching for repeated short prompts routed to L4 to reduce token cost and p95.
- Tiling/slotting: when autoscaling A100, prefer vertical scaling (more slots per node) to reduce cross-node KV fetches for long-context. This reduces p95 but increases memory per-node requirements.
- Fallback routing: implement a prioritized policy — 1) A100 pool, 2) L4 pool (if request <256 tokens), 3) remote hosted fallback model (last resort). Documented SLO for fallback: request must signal degraded mode in header for observability.
- Canary metrics: p95 latency, error rate, model output-quality sampling (random 0.5% of responses to an eval pipeline), and cost burn rate. Auto-rollback triggers: p95 > 600ms for more than 30 minutes OR error rate > 2x baseline.

Action items for Aerium:
- James/Sarah: confirm % long-context vs short-context per route (we used your high-level numbers; route-level split will refine node counts).
- Aerium: sign-off on canary windows (we propose 48h, start with 20% traffic).
- Redwood: we'll produce a final SKU sheet that maps routes -> preferred pool (A100/H100/L4) and an estimated monthly cost delta for 3 commitment levels.

Attachments included to this thread: [Attachment: sku_recommendation_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 85KB)]
